This Week in the Bay

Tuesday–Sunday, October 20–25, 2026 · the whole Bay Area

The last week of Litquake and the final weekend of SF Open Studios collide with peak Halloween-season oddity — a 20-foot Angkor bronze landing at the Asian Art Museum for the last time it will ever leave Cambodia, Joan Baez under a circus big top in Alameda, Joe Hisaishi conducting his own West Coast premiere, and a noise show that feeds you pancakes. Sectioned by type and ranked within. Use the day and region filters to narrow it down. Times were checked on each venue’s own page on Monday, October 19.

📚 Litquake’s closing week · Lit Crawl Sat 🎨 SF Open Studios, final weekend 👻 Peak Halloween season 🌜 Día de los Muertos programming begins ☀️ Rain Tue–Wed, then clear — Fri night is the stargazing night

Top 5 This Week

5 picks

The five best things happening across every category — chosen for rarity and variety, not five of a kind.

🌇
✦ Last time it leaves Cambodia
01 · OPENS FRIDAY

Vishnu’s Cosmic Ocean

Fri–Sun from Oct 23 · Asian Art Museum, Civic Center

The nearly 20-foot West Mebon Reclining Vishnu — Southeast Asia’s largest ancient bronze — newly conserved and shown at full scale for the first time in centuries. SF is the only West Coast venue, and the National Museum of Cambodia’s director says it is the last chance the masterpiece will ever be out of the country. Sunday brings a Cambodian Buddhist water blessing and Khmer dance.

Exhibition page →
🎪
★ CRITICS’ · SF Chronicle✦ Joan Baez
02 · FRI & SAT

The Soiled Dove — with Joan Baez

Fri 10/23 & Sat 10/24, doors 7:30pm · The Big Top, Radium Runway, Alameda

Vau de Vire Society’s immersive Barbary-Coast dinner-circus under a 12,000 sq ft Italian big top — aerialists, contortion, fire, a live orchestra, Frank Ferrante as Caesar, three courses hand-delivered by the cast — and Joan Baez performing live in a new theatrical role. A booking that will not come round again. 21+.

Fri tickets →

★ CRITICS’ · 7x7✦ Once a year · free
03 · SATURDAY · FREE

Lit Crawl SF 2026

Sat 10/24, 5–9pm in three phases · ~24 venues across the Mission

Litquake’s closing night and the world’s largest free pop-up literary event: 51 simultaneous readings you walk between — in bars, a coffee roaster, a sex shop, an internet provider’s office, the Mime Troupe HQ, Red Poppy and ATA. Tarot-and-spells poetics at 6:30, twenty pieces written in the hour before they’re read at 5:00, Bay Area journalists’ hottest takes at 8:00. No RSVP; just show up.

Full lineup →
🎻
✦ West Coast premiere
04 · THU–SAT

Hisaishi Conducts Hisaishi

Thu 10/22, Fri 10/23, Sat 10/24, 7:30pm · Davies Symphony Hall, Civic Center

Joe Hisaishi returns to the SF Symphony after four sold-out nights in 2024 to conduct the West Coast premiere of his own Concerto for Orchestra, a five-movement, 45-minute work the Symphony co-commissioned — plus further contemporary pieces. The composer of Spirited Away and Totoro on the podium for his own concert music. Limited availability.

★ CRITICS’ · SF Chronicle✦ Final weekend
05 · SAT & SUN · FREE

SF Open Studios — Weekend 5

Sat 10/24 & Sun 10/25, 11am–5pm · ~20 SF neighborhoods

The last of five weekends in ArtSpan’s month-long season — and the densest, most central neighborhood set of the lot: Chinatown, North Beach, Nob Hill, Russian Hill, Hayes Valley, Haight-Ashbury, the Richmond, the Sunset, Twin Peaks, West Portal and more. Hundreds of artists open their actual working studios. Free, running since 1975, now in its 52nd year.

Literary & Ideas

14 events

The densest literary week of the Bay Area year: Litquake’s final stretch (the festival runs Oct 8–24, with 28 events inside this window) plus the venue calendars underneath it. Litquake events are mostly free with a $10–15 suggested donation. Several are at capacity but take walk-ups — noted where known.

San Francisco
FREE · no RSVP · first come, first seated

Fifty-one simultaneous readings in three timed phases, in bars, a coffee roaster, a sex shop, an internet provider’s office and the Mime Troupe HQ. The Pelican Inn · Muir Beach

New musicSat 7:30pm

As Above, So Below — Echo Chamber Orchestra

First Presbyterian Church, 72 Kensington Rd · San Anselmo
North Bay
$30

The world premiere of Matt Rupert’s Other Worlds, a five-movement extension of Holst’s The Planets for chamber orchestra, electric guitar, alto flute and “enhanced percussion” — movements named Enceladus, Zoozve (Venus’s quasi-moon), Ceres, Europa and Theia. Paired with Beethoven’s Fourth Piano Concerto. An astronomy premiere on the same weekend as the telescope nights.

Notes & things to double-check

Times were read off each venue’s own page on Monday, October 19. Confirm before you commit on these: the Orchestre symphonique de Montréal on Sunday — the Symphony’s calendar says 7:30pm, the orchestra’s own page says 2pm; Audium’s per-date availability sits behind a JavaScript widget, so check which of Thu–Sat is actually on sale; Envelop SF publishes no times or prices outside its app (7:30pm is their standard); Terror Vault is sold out Friday and Saturday — Thursday and Sunday only; Haunted Oakland at Clio’s on Wednesday and Nik Sharma at Book Society on Thursday are both sold out; the Sherry Turkle talk and the Mrs. Dalloway’s memoir night are listed full but take walk-ups; and BAMPFA’s Sunday After Hours is sold out, rush only. Weather-dependent: Chabot’s and Foothill’s telescope nights are clear-sky-only — Friday’s forecast is mostly clear and Saturday’s is less certain, so check Chabot’s observatory weather page the same evening. A handful of cards show the category gradient instead of a photo because those venues ship no share image (SF Open Studios, Hisaishi, Fraenkel, Niles, the Stanford Theatre, Aftel, Envelop and a few others).

Deliberately deprioritized / skipped

Per your standing preferences: EDM and DJ club nights (DNA Lounge’s Halloween night, Daybreaker, Zombie Prom, Dom Dolla at Cow Palace), arena and amphitheatre concerts (Kacey Musgraves, Kehlani, Jungle), all sports, bar crawls (two Halloween pub crawls this week), brunch-as-event, networking mixers and sales expos. Pride- and identity-framed programming was pulled from the spotlight rather than hunted down: SFMOMA’s Kiki Ball, Big Gay Halloween at Great Star, the Frameline fall showcase titles, Oh, Mary! at the Curran, Chabot’s Science is a Drag and several Lit Crawl sessions all exist and are findable if you want them. Also checked and genuinely not on: TreasureFest (dormant — the organisers are “scouting our next location”), the Market Street Arts Festival and the CRANE light installation (both ended Oct 17–18), Brava’s block party (Oct 17), Bach Dancing & Dynamite, SF Ballet (in Idaho this week), Old First Concerts, CounterPulse, and the Oddities & Curiosities Expo, which is an expo.
